references.text: The immediate context: Jesus says that the disciples should not worry about life (the soul) regarding what they will eat, or about the body regarding what they will wear. Verse 23 gives the reason: life is more than food and the body more than clothing ([ref:Luk 12:22|Luke 12:22]).

The parallel text in Matthew's Sermon on the Mount, where Jesus gives the same teaching: "Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?" – almost word-for-word the same statement as in [ref:Luk 12:23|Luke 12:23] ([ref:Matt 6:25|Matthew 6:25]).

God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life. Human life (ψυχή) comes from God himself and is therefore far more valuable than that which sustains outward life ([ref:1 Mos 2:7|Genesis 2:7]).

"All that a man has, he will give for his life." Even Satan acknowledges that life (the soul) is worth more than all material things – something that underscores the point in [ref:Luk 12:23|Luke 12:23] ([ref:Job 2:4|Job 2:4]).

The psalmist praises God for the wonderful creation of the human body. The body that God has formed is far more than the clothes that cover it – God's care for what he has created is the basis for why we need not worry ([ref:Sal 139:13-16|Psalm 139:13–16]).

Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus says that the sparrows are not forgotten by God, and that the disciples are worth more than many sparrows. The argument is the same: God who gives what is greater (life, the body) will also give what is lesser (food, clothing) ([ref:Luk 12:6-7|Luke 12:6–7]).

Jesus continues by pointing to the lilies of the field, which neither spin nor weave, yet God clothes them more beautifully than Solomon. If God clothes the grass, how much more will he not clothe you – a further elaboration of the principle in verse 23 ([ref:Luk 12:27-28|Luke 12:27–28]).

Paul writes that bodily exercise is of little profit, but godliness is profitable for all things. This reflects Jesus' point that life is more than the physical and material ([ref:1 Tim 4:8|1 Timothy 4:8]).

"Seek first God's kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well." Because life is more than food and the body more than clothing, the priority should be God's kingdom – the material things will be provided by God ([ref:Matt 6:33|Matthew 6:33]).

"What does it profit a man if he gains the whole world but loses his soul?" Jesus again emphasizes that the soul (ψυχή) has infinitely greater value than all material things ([ref:Matt 16:26|Matthew 16:26]).
